A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same IRT-based framework for diagnosing LLM judges. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations of seven judges, human-alignment measurements, and prompt and rating-scale ablations across NLP and vision tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds comparisons with alternative reliability metrics, bootstrap estimates, and cross-model significance tests in Appendices F and G.

M1.justification: Both versions use the same GRM/2PL models, priors, NUTS inference, three prompt perturbations, and four diagnostic metrics. The added derivation and model-choice discussion do not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both evaluate SummEval, TopicalChat, HelpSteer-2, and ImageHub's CIG, MIE, and TIE subsets with the same task criteria. The added analyses use retained coverage; structural prompt reformulations and additional benchmarks are discussed as future work.

E2.justification: v1 reports Pearson correlations but only discusses McDonald's omega, Cohen's kappa, and Krippendorff's alpha as prior approaches. v2 evaluates all three across the benchmarks in Appendix F, Tables 7 and 9, substantially expanding the empirical comparator set. Pearson results are retained as Table 8.

E3.justification: Appendix F adds evaluation using omega across prompt variants and kappa/alpha against human ratings. The main experimental settings remain unchanged, including seven judges, temperature zero, prompt perturbations, rating-scale ablations, and GRM sampling configuration.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds analyses of diagnostic stability under resampling and differences across models. Existing TopicalChat and VIEScore prompt ablations, rating-scale comparisons, and score-level case analyses retain their results; their relocation does not constitute new analysis.

E5.justification: v2 adds bootstrap standard errors for CV and rho with B=1000 and Kruskal-Wallis tests across models for every benchmark-criterion pair (Tables 10 and 11). v1 already includes posterior-sampling details and Pearson significance markers, but lacks these diagnostic uncertainty and cross-model tests. Additional independent LLM runs are not established.

E6.justification: Original diagnostic, ablation, and Pearson values and plotted trajectories are unchanged. Tables 7 and 9-11 add extensive comparator results, standard errors, and reported cross-model significance at p<0.001 throughout. However, new Table 10 conflicts with retained Table 1: GPT-4o's TopicalChat naturalness rho is 0.80 versus 0.57, and CIG-SC/PQ entries are interchanged.

T1.justification: New Appendix A.1 derives GRM from a continuous logistic-noise response, defines threshold boundaries and exact-category probabilities, and introduces affine-invariance and parameter-count arguments for identifiability and cross-judge comparability. Section 3.4 also adds a Chebyshev-based argument for the CV threshold. This substantially expands the mathematical reasoning beyond v1's stated formulas.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the two-phase, four-metric diagnostic contribution and the distinction between calibration mismatch and validity gaps. Specifying seven judges and adding supporting analyses do not redefine the central claims.

C2.justification: Sections 3.3 and 8 explicitly limit Phase 1 to surface perturbations, qualify generalization beyond VIEScore, and identify unmodeled self-preference, position, and verbosity biases. Section 6.4 adds practical guidance, including possible post-hoc rescaling for NLP calibration differences. The principal interpretations of existing results remain.

D1.justification: The anonymized source-code placeholder becomes a specific IRT-Judge repository link in the abstract. Existing software versions, hardware, seed, and sampling settings are retained. The expanded fitting discussion primarily explains already documented choices.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting alternative IRT models, prompt sensitivity, reliability thresholds, and construct validity, including Bock, Masters, Sclar, and Cronbach and Meehl. These additions strengthen methodological positioning locally; the related-work section and overall relationship to prior research remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 corrects typos and cross-references, renames result and appendix headings, and expands explanations of GRM fitting. Practical Recommendations and Limitations become explicit sections, while Pearson comparisons and visualizations are reorganized into clearer appendices. Most existing main-text prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds four substantive tables for comparator metrics, bootstrap estimates, and significance tests, including a two-panel uncertainty table. Existing tables are relocated or renumbered, captions move above tables, and prompt templates are extensively reformatted into monospaced boxes. All seven figures retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: The added comparator evidence, explicit scope limitations, derivation, and concrete code link improve transparency. However, new Table 10 contains model and criterion mismatches with unchanged Table 1, undermining the added stability evidence. Appendix G also leaves the bootstrap resampling unit and refitting procedure unspecified. These unresolved problems make the net quality benefit uncertain despite the useful additions.
